title: NIST ASD: hydrogen 2–3 air wavelength 656.279 nm, beside resolved components
summary: The retrieved hydrogen table lists an unresolved 2–3 line at 656.279 ± 0.003 nm in air, and resolved components from 656.270970 nm to 656.285175 nm.
body: The NIST Atomic Spectra Database retrieval for H between 400 and 700 nm lists an observed air wavelength 656.279 nm, uncertainty 0.003 nm, for the transition whose levels are given only as 2 and 3. Relative intensity on that row is 500000. The Einstein A on that row is 4.4101 × 10^7 s^−1, accuracy AAA. The same retrieval lists resolved components: 656.270970 nm (uncertainty 0.000004) for 2p 2P* 1/2 to 3d 2D 3/2; 656.272483 nm (0.000003) for 2s 2S 1/2 to 3p 2P* 3/2; 656.277153 nm (0.000003) for 2s 2S 1/2 to 3p 2P* 1/2; and 656.285175 nm (0.000007) for 2p 2P* 3/2 to 3d 2D 5/2. The page says wavelengths of lines designated only by principal quantum numbers are for unresolved fine structure and are pertinent to solar-corona observations, and that laboratory relative intensities can differ by orders of magnitude. The 656.279 nm row is that unresolved listing. The four longer-decimal rows are the classified components on the same retrieval. Wavelengths are air wavelengths, as the column header says.
